grafts

grafts (graph forecasts for time series) is an interactive browser app for exploring aggregated time series, such as hierarchical, grouped and nested series, and their forecasts.

Installation

You can install the development version of grafts from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mitchelloharawild/grafts")

Usage

grafts explores time series stored in a tsibble whose keys have been aggregated with aggregate_key(). Any structure of keys works, whether hierarchical (State / Region), grouped (Purpose * State) or a mix of both.

library(grafts)
library(fable)

tourism_agg <- aggregate_key(
  tsibble::tourism, Purpose * (State / Region), Trips = sum(Trips)
)
grafts(tourism_agg)

grafts() makes an explorer, which opens in the viewer or a browser when printed in the console. The data stays in R, which serves each series only when it is drawn, so large collections of series open quickly. Like a Shiny app, the console waits while the explorer is open: press Ctrl+C (or Esc in RStudio and Positron) to stop it.

To also explore forecasts, pass a fable of forecasts for those series to forecasts. Each model’s forecasts and intervals are drawn after the data.

tourism_fc <- tourism_agg |>
  model(ets = ETS(Trips), snaive = SNAIVE(Trips)) |>
  forecast(h = "2 years")
grafts(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc)

Exploring

The explorer starts from the total of all series. Its left side shows the series graph, where each node is a series and its children sum to it. Clicking a node lists the ways it can be split, such as by Purpose or State, and choosing one adds those disaggregates to the graph. Below it, the dimension graph shows the structure of keys and highlights where the explorer is.

The right side plots the series being explored above its disaggregates, which can be shown as small multiples, overlaid, stacked (to see what each contributes to the total) or as seasonal plots. Clicking a time plot focuses that series, and hovering a node highlights its series wherever it is plotted. Right-clicking a node collapses its children, and shift-clicking pins it so series from different parts of the graph can be compared side by side.

Deploying

To serve the explorer from a server, add it to a plumber2 api with grafts_api(), which takes an explorer from grafts(). In a plumber2 file, such as for Posit Connect:

#* @plumber
function(api) {
  grafts_api(api, grafts(readRDS("tourism_agg.rds")))
}

In Docker, listen on all interfaces:

readRDS("tourism_agg.rds") |>
  grafts() |>
  grafts_serve(host = "0.0.0.0")

Responses are cached privately and revalidated, api/health answers load balancers, and the page’s links are relative, so the app works behind a proxy that mounts it under a path prefix. grafts_serve() listens on port 8000 (or GRAFTS_PORT/PORT), and has no sign-in, so keep anything private behind an authenticating proxy.

Several explorers can share one api by giving each a path, such as grafts_api(api, grafts(tourism_agg), path = "/tourism/").

Shiny

graftsOutput() and renderGrafts() put an explorer in a Shiny app. Small data are written into the page, and large data stay in R, which serves each series through the session as it is drawn.

The explorer tells the app what it shows, through inputs named after its output: input$ts_focus is the focused series (a one-row data frame of its keys), and ts_children, ts_pinned, ts_split, ts_view, ts_set, ts_theme and ts_measure follow the rest. graftsProxy() steers it from the server, and grafts_update() replaces its data without starting over: when the new data have the same series, the graph, focus, pins and views stay as they were.

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$ts <- renderGrafts(grafts(tourism_agg))

  observeEvent(input$ts_focus, {
    print(input$ts_focus)  # e.g. State = "Victoria", Region = NA
  })
  observeEvent(input$show_nsw, {
    graftsProxy("ts") |> grafts_focus(list(State = "New South Wales"))
  })
  observeEvent(input$refresh, {
    graftsProxy("ts") |> grafts_update(grafts(latest_data()))
  })
}

Embedding

Small collections of series can be explored without R, on a static web page such as a pkgdown site, a blog or GitHub Pages. An explorer from grafts() in an R Markdown or Quarto chunk, or in Shiny with renderGrafts(), is written into the page with every series, and a page can hold several explorers. grafts_save() writes one to a single HTML file.

tourism <- grafts(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc,
                  options = grafts_options(height = 600))
tourism  # in a chunk
grafts_save(tourism, "tourism.html")

grafts_options() chooses the views offered, the starting view and theme, and whether visitors’ choices persist, wherever the explorer goes. Whether series add up to their parents is detected, hiding the Stacked view and share scales for means.

grafts(tourism_agg, options = grafts_options(
  views = c("grid", "season"), theme = "dark", persist = FALSE
))

Every series is written into the page, so large collections are better served from R, in the console or with grafts_api(). Embedded explorers use the system’s UI font, unless the page loads Source Sans 3 as the app does.
